newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rise on U.S. interest rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rise on U.S. interest rate concerns.

text.p: Cetes rates rose across the yield curve at Mexico's primary treasury bill auction on Tuesday, as investors continued to respond to concerns that U.S. rate hikes may not be over, analysts said.
The one-month Cetes rate rose 47 basis points to 22.33 percent, less than expected by money market dealers.
According to a Reuters' survey of nine Cetes dealers, done before the auction results were released, interest rates on the 28-day Cetes were seen rising 80 basis points.
Analysts added that Mexican rates may have reached another ceiling.
"Rates are already at a new short-term ceiling," said one analyst who declined to be identified.
Mexican interest rates have been bouncing up and down in the past few weeks, pushed about by concerns over the direction of U.S. interest rates.
Mexican treasury bill rates rose across the yield curve at the auction last week as well, pushed up by concerns that interest rates were set to keep rising north of the border.
But for the two weeks before that they had fallen as the peso remained strong.

In early March, however, rates on the one-month Cetes rose a sharp 458 basis points over two auctions as markets began to digest the possibility that the U.S. Federal Reserve might begin to tighten monetary conditions there.
Those hikes came after Mexican interest rates had fallen for 10 straight weeks since the start of the year on weakening inflationary pressures in Mexico and good economic news.
The possibility that U.S. interest rates could keep rising will continue to guide Mexican rates, analysts said.
"Over the next few weeks, the market for emerging market debt will be dominated by U.S. Treasury rates," Salomon Brothers said in a recent report.
Demand this week was a strong 13.75 billion pesos, compared to the 9.81 billion pesos demand last week. There were 3.0 billion pesos on offer this week.
Demand was particulary strong for the 182-day paper, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 6.70. The bid-to-cover for the one-year paper was also high at 5.00.
Investors have been flooding into Mexico's money markets recently.

The Mexican Stock Exchange noted on Tuesday that foreign investment in the money market rose 18.73 percent to $3.576 billion in March from the month before. It is up 5.35 percent from the end of last year.
At the auction this week, the rate on 91-day paper rose 108 basis points to 22.98 percent. The yield on the 182-day paper rose 59 basis points to 22.99 percent.
The one-year paper was assigned at 23.94 percent compared with 23.90 percent last week.
